openApiTools.adminOnlyToast: Only workspace admins can import an API.
openApiTools.readOnlyNote: Only workspace admins can import, refresh, or change API sources. Every agent in the workspace can already call the tools listed here.
openApiTools.emptyBody: Point the platform at an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document and every operation in it becomes a tool your agents can call - no code to write.
openApiTools.importTitle: Import an API from its OpenAPI document
openApiTools.importIntro: Give the API a name, then paste the document or its URL. You will pick which operations to turn into tools on the next step.
openApiTools.stepReview: Step 2 of 2 · operations, base URL and auth
openApiTools.prefixHelp: Every generated tool is named <prefix>_<operation>, so two APIs with a "listUsers" never collide. Lowercase letters, digits, underscores.
openApiTools.specUrlHelp: Public http(s) URL of a JSON or YAML OpenAPI 3 / Swagger 2 document. URLs inside the platform's own network are refused.
openApiTools.nameRequired: Give the API a name first.
openApiTools.previewFailed: The document could not be read.
openApiTools.operationsFound: {count} operations found · tools will be named {prefix}_…
openApiTools.baseUrlHelp: Every operation's path is appended to this. Pre-filled from the document's first server when it declares one. Must be a public http(s) address.
openApiTools.baseUrlRequired: Enter the base URL the API is served from.
openApiTools.oauth2ClientIdPlaceholder: e.g. the API key from your developer portal app
openApiTools.oauth2ScopePlaceholder: space-separated, if the provider requires it
openApiTools.oauth2Help: The platform fetches a short-lived access token from the token URL, caches it until just before it expires, and sends it as Authorization: Bearer on every call. A 401 retries once with a fresh token.
openApiTools.oauth2Required: OAuth 2.0 needs a token URL, client ID and client secret.
openApiTools.secretPlaceholder: Stored encrypted; never shown again. {{secret.NAME}} references a workspace vault secret.
openApiTools.secretKeepPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the stored credential ({preview})
openApiTools.secretHelp: Encrypted at rest with the platform key and only decrypted for the duration of a call. Use {{secret.NAME}} to reference a workspace secret from the vault instead of pasting a value.
openApiTools.secretRequired: Enter the credential for the selected authentication.
openApiTools.selectAtLeastOne: Select at least one operation to import.
openApiTools.importedToast: "{name}" imported - {count} tools are live for your agents.
openApiTools.refreshTitle: Re-read the document and update the tools
openApiTools.loadToolsError: Could not load the tools of this API.
openApiTools.tryItHelp: The JSON an agent would send as the tool input. Runs the real request against the API with the stored credential and shows exactly what the agent would receive.
openApiTools.nameAndBaseUrlRequired: Name and base URL are both required.
openApiTools.prefixImmutableNote: The tool prefix ({prefix}) cannot change - agents may already rely on the generated tool names. To re-read the document itself, use Refresh.
openApiTools.deleteDialogBody: Its {count} generated tools disappear from every agent immediately and the stored credential is erased. This cannot be undone.

schedulePanel.noAgentsBody: Create an agent first — a schedule is a recurring job for one specific agent.
schedulePanel.skipsInARow: Skipped {count} in a row{reason} — often a sign each run takes longer than the interval.
schedulePanel.intervalHint: At least 1 minute. The scheduler checks once a minute.
schedulePanel.cronHint: Standard 5-field cron (or 6 with seconds). Example above: weekdays at 09:00. Cron schedules run at most every few minutes; use an interval for a fixed cadence.
schedulePanel.timezoneHint: IANA zone id, e.g. Asia/Kolkata. Blank means UTC.
schedulePanel.previewInvalid: Enter a valid interval (1 minute to 1 year) or cron.
schedulePanel.goalPlaceholder: What should the agent do every time this fires?

skillsPage.pageSubtitle: Packaged expertise your agents load only when a task needs it.
skillsPage.howItWorks: A skill is a set of instructions for one kind of task. Agents see only each skill's name and description; when a request matches, the agent loads the full instructions, and reads any bundled files only if it needs them. So you can add many skills without slowing agents down or raising cost on unrelated chats.

skillsPage.customEmptyMember: No custom skills yet. A workspace admin can add them.
skillsPage.builtInSubtitle: Included with the platform and on for every agent. Switch one off if you don't want agents to use it.
skillsPage.builtInReadOnly: Built-in skills can't be edited. To customise one, export it, change its name, and upload it as your own.
skillsPage.selectPrompt: Select a skill to read its instructions.
skillsPage.newHint: The name uses lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens (64 characters max). The description decides when agents use this skill, so say what it does and when to use it (1,024 characters max).
skillsPage.editHint: A skill's name can't be changed after it is created. To add or change bundled files, upload the skill again as a .zip.
skillsPage.savedNotice: Saved "{name}". Agents will use it from their next message.
